A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Neural Context Flow work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and Appendices A–F are readable and support comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: v3 reports original dynamical-system forecasting and adaptation experiments, benchmark comparisons, interpretability results and ablations.

after.justification: v5 retains those original experiments and reports additional noise, uncertainty, sample-efficiency, timing and pooling-strategy results.

M1.justification: The NCF-t1/t2 procedures, three-network architecture, objectives, Algorithms 1–4 and adaptation rule remain unchanged. The three pooling strategies already existed in v3; v5 relocates and evaluates them. Revised experimental configurations do not introduce a new method.

E1.justification: All seven physical systems are retained. v5 adds Gaussian-corrupted LV adaptation trajectories and extends explicit beyond-training-horizon uncertainty diagnostics across the six comparison systems; v3's corresponding uncertainty illustration covered LV and SM. Trajectory-count and environment-count sweeps do not add datasets.

E2.justification: v5 adds One-Per-Environment (OPE) to the SP comparison, which previously evaluated OFA and NCF. It also evaluates OFA and OPE against NCF in the new BT sample-efficiency study. CAVIA and CoDA remain the comparators in the unchanged six-system comparison.

E3.justification: v5 introduces ensemble-based uncertainty metrics and near-zero filtering, trajectory-count sweeps, fixed-RK4 timing tests and a controlled pooling comparison. The SP training description changes from NCF-t2 with 500 outer and 20 inner iterations to NCF-t1 with 12000 epochs. Since v3 elsewhere already labels SP as NCF-t1, this establishes revised documentation, not an unambiguous history of rerunning the experiment.

E4.justification: v5 adds noisy LV parameter-identification tests, quantitative uncertainty/error diagnostics, SP and BT sample-efficiency studies, environment-scaling measurements and a controlled comparison of pooling strategies. These test robustness, data requirements, computational scaling and design choices beyond v3's retained pool-size, context-size and architecture ablations.

E5.justification: v3 already includes error bars and candidate-trajectory mean/standard-deviation plots. v5 adds empirical three-sigma intervals and coverage reporting, specifies ten Gaussian-noise seeds and three repeats for pooling and SP validation studies, and reports across-epoch timing variability. These additions do not establish increased run counts for the retained benchmark results.

E6.justification: The six-system comparison is numerically unchanged between v3 Table 1 and v5 Table 2. SP scores and architecture-ablation values are revised: the LV full-NCF ablation row changes from 1.28/0.80 to 6.73/7.92 for InD/adaptation MSE, all times 10^-5. v5 also adds uncertainty, noise, timing, sample-efficiency and pooling outcomes. Revised SP settings prevent a same-setting performance interpretation, and v5 Tables 1 and 7 contain unreconciled SP values.

T1.justification: v3 invokes the prior CAMEL identifiability result and illustrates parameter recovery empirically. v5 adds Proposition 2, explicit affine-system assumptions, an extended proof and parameter-recovery derivations in Appendix A.2. The existing Taylor/JVP proof and optimization convergence theorem are retained.

C1.justification: v5 explicitly adds an affine-system identifiability proof to the introduction's contributions. The central claims about contextual self-modulation, interpretability, uncertainty estimation, benchmark provision and best OoD performance on five of six comparison problems remain.

C2.justification: v5 adds substantive applicability qualifications: OPE can become preferable with sufficient data and time, noisy identification deteriorates outside the training convex hull, and uncertainty coverage requires problem-specific interpretation. It explains pooling-strategy convergence differences and removes proximal optimization from the SM performance explanation, retaining the higher-order Taylor interpretation.

D1.justification: v5 adds a PyTorch implementation link, OFA/OPE architecture and budget details, SP generation/testing details, and instructions for the new analyses. Most network specifications, optimizers, solver settings, hardware information and JAX listings are retained through the relocation of v3 Appendix B to v5 Appendix D.

R1.justification: v5 expands positioning around parametric PDEs and foundation models, adding works such as Herde and Takamoto, and cites Duan for affine identification and Serrano for uncertainty evaluation. Arjovsky, He and Portwood references are removed. The central positioning relative to CoDA, CAVIA and CAMEL remains.

P1.justification: The introduction is substantially rewritten and reordered. Pooling-strategy explanations move from the main text to Appendix A.6, the datasets/ablations/implementation appendices are reordered, an appendix contents page is added, and Broader Impact becomes an Ethics Statement. Extensive prose editing accompanies this reorganization.

P2.justification: v5 adds figures and tables for noise, uncertainty, sample efficiency, scaling and pooling. The SP table gains OPE and revised column scaling; its training plot gains normalized progress and validation curves. Figure 25 combines retained LV plots with new SM examples, while conference formatting substantially reflows the displays.

improvement.justification: v5 improves assessment of NCF through OPE controls, sample-efficiency and timing studies, noise tests and pooling ablations, making its useful operating conditions clearer. However, Appendix A.2 does not justify inferring Taylor equality on open neighborhoods from zero sampled loss; Eq. (26) normalizes candidate dispersion by trajectory length N rather than candidate count p; and SP values in Tables 1 and 7 remain unreconciled. These issues temper the empirical gains and limit confidence in the added theoretical and uncertainty claims.
